name: fatḥah
fn: A short, open "a" sound — like the "a" in "cat".

name: kasrah
fn: A short "i" sound — like the "i" in "sit".

name: ḍammah
fn: A short "u" sound — like the "u" in "put".

name: fatḥatayn
fn: An "-an" sound added at the end of a word — the most common tanwīn in everyday words.

name: kasratayn
fn: An "-in" sound, marking a word as grammatically indefinite and genitive — often heard after a preposition like فِي ("in") or مِنْ ("from").

name: ḍammatayn
fn: An "-un" sound, marking a word as grammatically indefinite and the subject of a sentence.

name: fatḥah + alif
fn: Stretches the short "a" into a long "aa", held about twice as long — like the "a" in "father".

name: kasrah + yāʾ
fn: Stretches the short "i" into a long "ee" — like the "ee" in "see".

name: ḍammah + wāw
fn: Stretches the short "u" into a long "oo" — like the "oo" in "food".

name: sukūn
fn: marks a consonant with no vowel of its own; closes a syllable

name: shaddah
fn: doubles (geminates) the consonant; always carries a vowel or tanwīn
